chunks: Ahmad ibn Mihrān, from ʿAbd al-ʿAẓīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥasanī, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) said to me, while we were on the road on the night of Friday: “Recite, for it is the night of Friday, the Qur'an.”

So I recited: “Indeed, the Day of Decision is the appointed time for them all. The Day when no patron shall avail another patron in anything, nor shall they be helped, except the one upon whom Allah has mercy.”
Then Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) said: “By Allah, we are the ones upon whom Allah has had mercy, and by Allah, we are the ones whom Allah has excepted; rather, we avail on their behalf.”

key_terms.اسْتَثْنَى اللَّهُ: Allah made an exception, indicating those excluded from the general rule
key_terms.رَحِمَ اللَّهُ: Allah showed mercy, referring here to those granted divine mercy
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ الْجُمُعَةِ: the night of Friday, highlighted here as a time for Qur'an recitation
key_terms.مَوْلًى: a patron, protector, or one closely connected to another
key_terms.مِيقَاتَهُمْ: their appointed time, the fixed moment set for all of them
key_terms.نُغْنِي عَنْهُمْ: we avail on their behalf, meaning to benefit or suffice for them
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْفَصْلِ: the Day of Decision, the final day of separation and judgment

ai.seo_question: Who are those excepted by Allah’s mercy in the verses about the Day of Decision?
ai.summary: This hadith presents an Imamī commentary on the Qur'anic exception in the verses about the Day of Decision. Imām Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) identifies the Ahl al-Bayt (عليهم السلام) as those singled out by divine mercy and exception, indicating their special role in benefiting others on that day.
